data.narrative:
Zeitview, a Series D-stage autonomous systems company founded by Dan Burton, operates within the Drones & Autonomous sector. The broader comp universe includes eight private firms in this space—including Wayve, Waymo, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—though no public comparables exist. Zeitview has raised $174M to date.

The Peer-Median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage peers meeting valuation-tier filters; a broader sector median would risk obscuring meaningful differences across company maturity and capital structures. Consequently, valuation relies on Stage-Progression analysis, which applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D-to-subsequent-stage transitions against the $174M total raised proxy. This method implies a valuation of $261M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $222M (low) to $300M (high), centered on $261M. Key uncertainties remain substantial: the single-method reliance reflects genuine scarcity of narrow peer data rather than methodological confidence, and the stage-progression multiplier assumes Zeitview follows conventional Series D dynamics—an assumption that may not hold for frontier autonomous systems where funding patterns and exit timing diverge from software norms. Prospective investors should weight this range as preliminary pending access to comparable transaction data or near-term financing signals from the peer set.
